links.outcome: Readability and PEMAT-P understandability of AI-generated vs web radiation information; effect of 6th-grade prompt
links.effect: Understandability score ≥70: 7.5% of web pages; at normal level 50.0% ChatGPT-4o, 78.6% Gemini; at 6th-grade level all texts except Copilot (26.7%) 100%. Actionability ≥70 was 0% for AI texts.
links.quote: At the 6th-grade level, all AI-generated texts exceeded this threshold.

links.outcome: Effect of prompting for 6th-grade reading level on readability and understandability of AI texts
links.effect: With 6th-grade prompt, jReadability scores rose (e.g., ChatGPT-4o 2.8 to 3.3, Gemini 3.5 to 3.8) and understandability ≥70 reached 100% for most chatbots vs web pages 7.5%; Copilot remained 26.7%.
links.quote: However, when the prompt “Explain it at a 6th-grade level” was used, all AI chatbots—except for Copilot—produced texts that were easier to read and comprehend than web-based information, regardless of whether the version was paid or free.

links.effect: Normal PEMAT-P understandability means: web 41.9, ChatGPT-4o 69.7, Copilot 43.3, Gemini 78.3; 6th-grade: web 41.9, ChatGPT-4o 87.5, Copilot 57.4, Gemini 87.5.
links.quote: Comparisons among the three AI chatbots, ChatGPT, Copilot, and Gemini, revealed clear differences in text quality.

links.effect: PEMAT-P understandability ≥70: web 7.5%; normal ChatGPT-4o 50.0%, Gemini 78.6%; 6th-grade ChatGPT variants and Gemini 100.0%, Copilot 26.7%.
links.quote: For the proportion of texts with PEMAT-P Understandability scores ≥70, ChatGPT-4o (n=7, 50.0%) and Gemini (n=11, 78.6%) at the Normal level, and ChatGPT-4o (n=15, 100.0%), ChatGPT-4o mini (n=15, 100.0%), ChatGPT-o1 (n=15, 100.0%), ChatGPT-o1 mini (n=15, 100.0%), and Gemini (n=14, 100.0%) at the 6th grade level showed significantly higher proportions compared to other groups ( P <0.05).

links.effect: jReadability means: web 1.8; normal AI 2.4–3.5; 6th-grade AI 3.1–4.3, with 6th-grade outputs easier than web-based materials.
links.quote: The results showed that, especially when using the prompt “Explain at a 6th-grade level”, AI-generated texts were easier to understand and had lower Japanese-language complexity than web-based materials.

links.effect: At standard level, 50.0% of ChatGPT-4o and 78.6% of Gemini texts scored ≥70 for understandability; at 6th-grade level, 100% of ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-4o mini, ChatGPT-o1, ChatGPT-o1 mini, and Gemini scored ≥70 (P<0.05).
links.quote: For the proportion of texts with PEMAT-P Understandability scores ≥70, ChatGPT-4o (n=7, 50.0%) and Gemini (n=11, 78.6%) at the Normal level, and ChatGPT-4o (n=15, 100.0%), ChatGPT-4o mini (n=15, 100.0%), ChatGPT-o1 (n=15, 100.0%), ChatGPT-o1 mini (n=15, 100.0%), and Gemini (n=14, 100.0%) at the 6th grade level showed significantly higher proportions compared to other groups ( P <0.05).

links.effect: Difficult responses were lower with ChatGPT-o1 (13.3%), Copilot (13.3%), and Gemini (7.1%) at 6th-grade level, compared to webpages (100.0%), ChatGPT-4o (100.0%), ChatGPT-o1 (93.3%), and ChatGPT-o1 mini (100.0%) at normal level.
links.quote: For responses rated as more difficult than “somewhat difficult” by jReadability, the proportion of difficult responses was lower with ChatGPT-o1 (n=2, 13.3%), Copilot (n=2, 13.3%), and Gemini (n=1, 7.1%) at the 6th-grade level.
